source.prompt: A European starling (Sturnus vulgaris), one adult standing on the ground, side-on pose, wings folded tight. Realistic proportions: 21 cm long, a stocky body, a short square tail, a long pointed straight yellow bill, a flat head, pinkish legs. Glossy black plumage with a green and purple sheen, the body speckled with small white and buff spots, buff edges on the wing feathers. Three toes forward and one back. No base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: Scaled to 0.21 m bill to tail. The preview (a clean stocky starling: flat head, long pointed bill) kept and pitched 4 degrees nose-down to a near-level ground stance; the generated legs, long tail and wingtips cut and replaced by pinkish procedural legs and a short square tail of 6 cm 10 degrees below level; pointed flight cards. Colours: glossy black, purple-tinged on the head and neck shading to green-black on the body; white (below) and buff (above) spots as whole faces decided at each face centre and weakened on faces larger than a spot; blackish folded wings with buff fringes (lod0); buff tail tip and trailing edges on the cards; yellow bill. Triangles: lod0 998 = 833 body + 165 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod1 400 = 315 body + 85 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod2 120 = 93 body + 27 legs, tail, cards, eyes. GLB 177,264 bytes. lod_m is a suggestion.

rig: bird rig template of the Steller's jay (tools/build_stellersjay.py; drawn with client/src/animalModels.js RIG.stjay's constants): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 / LEG_B 2 procedural legs (pivot at the knee), TAIL 3 procedural tail (pivot at the rump), HEAD 6 (head and neck, pivot at the base of the neck), WING_L/R 4/5 and HAND_L/R 9/10 flight cards that collapse into the shoulder on pose; extras.rig {kind 'bird', wing (shoulder), tail (rump), head (neck base), length_m}; no skin
accuracy_notes: Built 2026-11-06. Reads as a starling: dark, glossy, speckled, a long yellow bill and short tail. Still open: the body faces are larger than real spots, so the speckle on the breast is a sprinkle of pale faces rather than fine dots; the sheen is a fixed purple-to-green tint, not view-dependent; the tail is a flat plate, thin side-on.
